title: A/B TEST BUDGET
subtitle: Same engine, different stakes — every test costs real traffic.

intro.headline: You have traffic for 18 variants
intro.body: Each tile is a landing-page variant: headline style across, layout across the other axis. Testing one costs a slice of live traffic you cannot get back. Find the best converting variant before you run out.

strategies.bayesianLike: Iterating on your best variant — that is exploitation.
strategies.randomSearch: Sampling widely across the design space.
strategies.mixed: Balancing new ideas against refining a winner.

foundGlobal.title: Best variant found
foundGlobal.body: You landed on {bestValue}% conversion at ({bestX}, {bestY}) in {reveals} tests. Multi-armed bandit algorithms formalise what you just did: shift traffic toward variants that are winning, but keep a trickle going to the others in case you are wrong.

foundLocal.title: Left money on the table
foundLocal.body: You shipped {bestValue}% but {globalValue}% existed. With {exploitPercent}% of tests clustered near an early winner, you optimised a hill you happened to land on. This is why teams that only ever A/B-test small tweaks plateau — local search cannot find a design it never tries.

scattered.title: Thorough, and expensive
scattered.body: You covered {uniqueRegions} regions across {reveals} tests to find {bestValue}%. Correct, but every slice of traffic sent to a bad variant is revenue spent on information. A bandit would have cut the losers early and reached the same answer in about {optimalReveals}.

titleScreen.instructions: Click a variant to send it traffic. You have 18 slices.
